text: The onboarding write is served on the partner base as POST or PATCH /partners under /api/recovery/partner/v1 with right C, the create right of the CRUDA row of RW-AGENCYMG, and its method, path, request element and operation name stay placeholders until the owner publishes them.
why: FEAT-PRM-01 needs a write that no inventory publishes: TSD S9 T-A.1 lists API-S9-001 and the five instruction operations only, and the ownership rows give the same six. The FSD names the partner and agency manager as primary and T6.1 gives that role CRUDA on the Partner portal, so C is the right the write needs, but no operation names it. Declaring a published method and path as fixed would invent an interface.

impact: The app story builds the command behind the base on Day 1, the baseline declares the shape with the placeholder, and no endpoint outside the ownership rows enters a document

text: The fee schedule, the service levels and the scope of a partner are the versioned reference data of FEAT-PRM-02 and not columns of the panel: this story records the partner, its type, its panel state and its contract end, and no field links a partner to a version of its terms.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 gives partner seven fields, none of them a fee schedule, a service level, a scope or a contract start, and FSD S9 A2.2 keeps every panel, fee schedule and service level as versioned reference data. Adding a link column or a term property would be a business value and a schema change invented by the builder.

text: The decision record of an onboarding is written through the local decision-record library on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 before the partner row changes, and a failed write leaves the panel unchanged with MSG-P7-003, which is the whole of legacy AC2.
why: TSD S9 T2 states that the service writes the decision log entry before any change and that this module acts on events from P3 and writes through the decision log; FSD S9 A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-S9-001-02 repeats the behaviour. DP-03 is in the pattern set with the H row RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, so the library is the mechanism and no other is chosen.

impact: The record and the row commit together or not at all, AC2 is provable on the stub, and the central ledger of rwb-decision sits behind the local record

text: partner_user is S9's third table and holds the portal user of a firm; the module TSD publishes field definitions for partner and partner_instruction only, so this story names the table, inserts one row where portal access is requested, scopes it as NFR-050 gives it and leaves its field list to the DB story.
why: The ownership rows give S9 three tables, and partner_user is one of them, so the table is this service's and no other service may hold it; TSD S9 T3.1 is silent on its columns and invents nothing. FSD S9 A2.1.3.2 lists partner and partner_instruction fields only, so no field can be named without a gap.

text: Onboarding publishes no event: InstructionIssued (EV-20) and PartnerResultSubmitted (EV-21) belong to the instruction and result stories of this service, and the DP-09 outbox and inbox library that relays them is recorded rather than added to the metadata row.
why: The event catalogue gives the service two events, one published when an instruction is issued and one consumed from the partner portal, and neither is a fact of onboarding a partner. DP-09 is absent from the pattern set of this key, so the library row RWB-PLT-TE006-CON cannot be added without inventing a metadata value.

The plan gives this key an empty C row and no source publishes the operation name.

text: Staff screens reach rwb-partner through the gateway-bff composite route and partner firms reach it through the partner gateway on FAPI 2.0; the composite route is the DP-19 dependency H RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the partner gateway is an edge capability that no pattern row and no dependency row carries.
